Full notes saved to `C:\Users\shubh\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-shubh-Projects--claude\d3907c69-e0f0-457b-bec9-6a76569849b3\scratchpad\ba\literary\sources.md`. Downloads are in `...\ba\literary\dl\` and scripts in `...\ba\literary\tools\`. I checked everything on 2026-10-20 against BibleAtlas main `5296d48`. I fetched first and never edited the clone.

## 1. What the app already has (main 5296d48)

**Layers.** None of the note kinds covers parallelism, chiasm, inclusio, anthropomorphism, personification, merism, hyperbole, metaphor or character contrast.

In the text and evidence of the 3,099 notes:
- anthropopatheia or anthropomorphism: 0
- "after the manner of men": 2 (genesis-18-21, acts-2-6)
- personification: 4
- chiasm: 0; introversion: 0; merism: 0; hyperbole: 0
- metaphor: 3; simile: 3
- "parallel": 18. Of these, 15 mean a parallel passage. Only 4 evidence lines rely on Hebrew parallelism to fix a meaning (psalm-33-6, psalm-68-1, jeremiah-25-26, hebrews-7-2). None shows parallelism to the reader as a device.
- "contrast": 87
- pun or paronomasia: 140

**Bullinger citations.** There are 536. The 419 Companion Bible cites carry no `at`. The 117 Figures of Speech cites name 23 figures, mostly Paronomasia (52) and Ploce (23). Anthropopatheia appears twice (genesis-4-9 and john-1-41; I checked both in the e-text and both are real) and Hyperbole once (revelation-18-5). So FoS is already used, but only to support wordplay and allusion notes.

**Stored voices.** Source is `LetsChurch/lets.church` @ `71f6f0f`.
- Wesley names the devices fairly often: "after the manner of men" 34 times, metaphor 76, hyperbole 9, irony 13.
- Henry's Concise rarely names a device ("after the manner of men" 5 times, metaphor 0).
- On Genesis 6:6, Henry says "they are used after the manner of men, and do not mean that God can change". Wesley says "These are expressions after the manner of men".
- Character pairs come up in their own words. Henry on Genesis 4: "The offerings of Cain and Abel were different". Wesley on Genesis 4:4: "Cain was a wicked man, but Abel was a righteous man".
- Aquifer, already in the app, has contrast 243, metaphor 101, inclusio or bookend 20 and chiasm 9.

## 2. Bullinger, *Figures of Speech Used in the Bible* (1898)

The title page says 1898. The preface in both scans is dated "November, 1899". It is public domain in the US.

**Digital copies:**
- **archive.org `figuresofspeechu00bull`** (https://archive.org/details/figuresofspeechu00bull): Princeton scan, marked `NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT`, 1,168 images. The OCR text file is 2,551,514 bytes, sha1 `e5a4296364d1e178d1fd9b53017b89f191ee4482`. It has all 7 indexes, including Index IV of Structures. Layers already links to this copy.
- **archive.org `cu31924029277047`**: Cornell scan, "no known copyright restrictions". OCR sha1 `19c652aa4b2d44f5e422bf4efee8d56a92fb8a48`.
- **archive.org `figuresofspeechu0000unse`**: a third scan. The 1968 Baker reprints there are lending-only.
- **Clean e-text on GitHub:** `darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books` @ `4017a67481e0de6027216bbdf3fc5d42c9c289d5`, file `Bullinger - Figures of Speach.book.zip` (blob `fa7da80c`). It is a SQLite version of a BibleSupport e-Sword module. The repo has no license and also holds copyrighted books (Keener, McGee, Leupold).
- **Also on GitHub:** a PDF in `otseng/UniqueBible_PDF`.
- **Not available:**
  - CCEL has only Bullinger's *Commentary on Revelation* and calls him an "ultra-dispensationalist".
  - Wikisource has only an author page with red links.
  - Project Gutenberg has only *Witness of the Stars*.
  - levendwater shows page images.
  - HathiTrust blocked scripted requests (HTTP 403).
  - Accordance and SwordSearcher are commercial.
- **Structured datasets:** GitHub search found no structured FoS dataset beyond this module.

**How the book is organised.** It has three Divisions:
- Omission
- Addition (including Parallelism and Correspondence)
- Change (including Simile, Metaphor, Prosopopoeia and Anthropopatheia)

There are 5 appendixes and 7 indexes.

The number of figures depends on how you count:
- Accordance says 217.
- The scan's analytical contents list 194 main headings.
- The e-text has 203 sections.
- Companion Bible Appendix 6 lists "The 181".

**How cleanly references come out.**
- In the e-text every reference is a `bcv(book,chapter,verse)` link: 11,386 links, starting at 7,304 distinct verses.
- Structures keep their letters, their indentation and the italic mark on the matching member. There are 194 lettered structure blocks (63 under Correspondence, 44 under Parallelism).
- The e-text lacks the indexes.
- Quality check: I looked up 500 random six-word runs in the scan OCR and found 345 word for word. I traced 5 misses by hand, and each came from OCR noise in the scan, not from errors in the e-text.
- The 1898 OCR itself uses Roman chapter numbers, and a regex finds only 6,796 references in it. So the scans work as a check, not as the source to parse.

**Samples** (links / distinct verses inside each figure's section):

| Figure | Links / verses | What is inside |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropopatheia | 998 / 779 | Sorted by body part and feeling: face 42, eyes 31, repentance 23, remembering 18, smelling 14, arm of the Lord and more |
| Parallelism | 59 / 59 | 7 kinds: synonymous, antithetic, synthetic, alternate, repeated, extended, introverted |
| Correspondence | 117 / 99 | Alternate (simple 18, extended 44, repeated 5), introverted 12, complex 19; credits Thomas Boys |
| Antithesis | 35 / 30 | Plus Enantiosis 5 |
| Merismos | 5 / 5 | Bullinger's "Distribution", not the modern merism. "Going out and coming in" sits under Synecdoche, and "heaven and earth" is not treated as a figure |
| Synecdoche | 821 / 737 | Includes "whole for part" subsections |
| Prosopopoeia | 220 / 198 | |
| Hyperbole | 133 / 121 | |
| Metaphor | 47 / 46 | Narrow: "A is B" only. Implied comparisons are Hypocatastasis (14) and Allegory (29) |
| Simile | 85 / 83 | |
| Epanadiplosis | 42 | Line-level bookend |
| Climax | 12 | |

**A rule point.** FoS's history of parallelism names De Rossi, "a learned Jew of the sixteenth century", whose chapter Lowth translated in his Isaiah dissertation. The app must never cite De Rossi.

## 3. The Companion Bible (1909 to 1922)

It is public domain in the US. Bullinger died in 1913, and his associates finished it.

**Copies:**
- **archive.org per-book scans and OCR:** `thecompanionbible_202504` (57 OCR files), `appendixes_202504`, `CompanionBibleOT` (Haywood's 2005 scan edition), and the Kregel `companionbible0000ewbu`. None states a license.
- **StudyLight** (`/commentaries/eng/bul/`): says "These files are public domain." It has the notes only, without the structures.
- **levendwater:** all 198 appendixes as HTML.
- **GitHub `otseng/UniqueBible_Commentaries` @ `4b77d86`:** notes as SQLite, 1,236 chapter rows. It has no license and sits beside copyrighted works. The structures are flattened, with the letters lost. An earlier voices check found Gen 1:1 notes missing and "a" and "=" turned into ".".
- **SwordSearcher's forum** says the structures "are difficult to create in a text module".

**Structures.**
- The OCR has about 2,300 type labels (Old Testament 1,690, New Testament 622). About 300 of these are "Division" outlines, which leaves roughly 2,000 alternations and introversions.
- Letters and bars survive in the OCR with noise. For example, Genesis 2:4-25 reads "C[d]s." where the book has "C | d | 8.". The italic matching letters are not marked.
- Character pairs exist inside some structures:
  - 1 Samuel 1:1 to 4:1 is a "Repeated Alternation" of "Elkanah's son, Samuel" against "The sons of Eli / Eli and his sons". This is Samuel versus Eli's sons in Bullinger's own outline.
  - The note on 1 Samuel 1:2 says "Hannah = Grace. Peninnah = Pearl. Note the Fig. Antimetabole."

**Appendix 6.** It gives 181 figures with one-line definitions and about 332 example references. Its forms of Correspondence and Parallelism are good plain definitions.

**Figure tags in the notes.** There are 4,025 "Figure of speech X" tags on 3,506 verses. The most relevant: Anthropopatheia 236, Prosopopoeia 58, Metaphor 23, Hyperbole 13, Simile 12.

**Bullinger's stance.** He passes the rule as written. He held every word inspired, was secretary of the Trinitarian Bible Society, and opposed the "Elohistic and Jehovistic theories". But he also held:
- ultradispensationalism (H. A. Ironside called it "absolutely Satanic")
- soul sleep (the Companion Bible repunctuates Luke 23:43; FoS does not treat that verse)
- the gap theory
- a Wednesday crucifixion, with four men crucified alongside Jesus
- the "Gospel in the stars"
- he was a member of the flat-earth society (the Universal Zetetic Society) and chaired its meeting on 7 March 1905

Eusebius (*Church History* 6.37) records a synod that won back Arabians who taught that the soul "dies and perishes with the body" until the resurrection. That is a judgment call for the founder, not a breach of the rule as written.

## 4. Older believing writers

All of these are public domain. Except Keach, none has a copy on GitHub or Project Gutenberg, so each needs a mirror branch.

**Robert Lowth**
- Works: *Lectures* (Gregory translation 1787; editions 1816, 1829, 1847) and *Isaiah* with its Preliminary Dissertation (1778).
- Copies: archive.org `lecturesonsacred00lowtrich` (1829, OCR sha1 `25a915bc`), `bim_eighteenth-century_lectures-on-the-sacred-p_lowth-robert_1787_1` and `_2`, `isaiahnewtransla1834lowt` (sha1 `bc22f1e9`).
- Stance: he says the sacred poems are "justly attributed to the inspiration of the Holy Spirit".
- What he gives: Lecture XIX sets out the three kinds of parallelism (synonymous, antithetic, synthetic).
- Cautions:
  - Cite Lowth's own words only. The editions carry notes by Michaelis, and Stowe's notes cite De Wette, Eichhorn and Gesenius.
  - In the 1829 edition the Bible examples are in Latin.

**John Jebb**, *Sacred Literature* (1820)
- Copy: `sacredliterature00jebb` (sha1 `b5d49a08`).
- Stance: he calls God "the inspirer of both portions of the Sacred Volume".
- What he gives: he names "the introverted parallelism", in an order "from flanks to centre".

**Thomas Boys**, *Tactica Sacra* (1824) and *A Key to the Book of Psalms* (1825)
- Copies: `tactica-sacra` (sha1 `bca42087`), `10353478bsb`, `akeytobookpsalm00boysgoog` (sha1 `cec0c7d8`).
- Stance: he writes of those "who acknowledge the inspiration of the Bible". He made the Trinitarian Bible Society's Portuguese Bible.
- Missing: Bullinger's 1890 edition of Boys's *A Key to the Psalms* was not found anywhere.

**John Forbes**, *The Symmetrical Structure of Scripture* (1854)
- Copy: `symmetricalstruc00forbiala` (sha1 `4f0d3281`).
- Stance: his contents include "Plenary Inspiration claimed by Scripture itself".

**T. H. Horne**, *Introduction*, editions 1818 to 1846 only
- Copy example: `introductionto02horn` (1823). It has chapters on figurative language (including "the anthropopathy" and "the prosopopoeia") and on parallelism (gradational, antithetic, constructive, introverted).
- Caution: the 1856 volume was rewritten by Samuel Davidson, who was forced to resign over it.

**Keach and De Laune**, *Tropologia* (1681)
- This is the best licensed find: GitHub `textcreationpartnership/A37483` @ `e290ad310b3c0386b57fce98f8fe489c7679a06f`, under "Creative Commons 0 1.0 Universal".
- Stance: Keach helped call the 1689 Baptist Assembly.
- What it covers:
  - "Metaphors Translated from Man to God": members, affections and actions ascribed to God
  - prosopopoeia
  - synecdoche (including of the whole)
  - hyperbole and allegory
  - hundreds of metaphors and "express similitudes"

**Commentators already on the cite list as witnesses.** I fetched Bible Hub pages to check:
- **Genesis 6:6.**
  - Calvin: "This figure ... is called anthropopatheia" and "the Spirit accommodates himself to our capacity".
  - Benson: "after the manner of men, by the same figure of speech whereby eyes, ears, hands, and feet are ascribed to God".
  - Pulpit also comments.
  - Henry, Wesley and FoS agree.
  - Result: widely agreed.
- **Proverbs 10:1** (antithetic): Clarke cites "Bishop Lowth"; JFB, Keil and Delitzsch, and Pulpit agree.
- **Isaiah 6:10** (chiasm): JFB ("the reverse order"), Keil and Delitzsch ("inverse order"), FoS, and Jebb with Boys.
- **Psalm 98:8:**
  - Gill: "a prosopopoeia".
  - Calvin: "feeling is ascribed to things inanimate".
  - Caution: on the same Calvin page, "a most beautiful prosopopoeia" is footnote [113] by the 1840s translator, not Calvin.
- **Matthew 19:24:** Ellicott calls it "apparent hyperbole". Most others, FoS included, call it a proverb.
- **Matthew 7:6:** FoS and Jebb, who credits Bengel (on the cite list) and Hammond.
- **Genesis 9:6:** no pre-1931 witness to a chiasm found.
- **Character foils:** Augustine, *City of God* XV.1: "Cain ... belonged to the city of men; ... Abel ... belonged to the city of God."

**Excluded or flagged:**
- **Milton S. Terry:** his 1901 book says of the Pentateuch "we find nothing to show that Moses was the author of any one of them".
- **Origen:** condemned in 543 and 553.
- **Novatian:** a schismatic.
- **J. D. Michaelis:** not confirmed as holding the whole Bible true.
- **Davidson's 1856 Horne volume.**
- **Lund (1942):** after the public-domain line.
- **Latter-day Saint chiasm projects.**
- **Jewish scholars:** already on the avoid list.

## 5. A modern option that passes the rule

**unfoldingWord Translation Notes**, at `git.door43.org/unfoldingWord/en_tn`.
- Where it lives: Gitea, not GitHub, so it would need a mirror.
- License: CC BY-SA 4.0.
- Statement of faith: "the only inspired, inerrant, sufficient, authoritative Word of God".
- What it has: per-verse figure tags keyed to the Hebrew and Greek words.
  - Psalms: metaphor 1,182, parallelism 297, personification 133, hyperbole 68, merism 58.
  - Genesis: 1,370 tags.
- Why it matters: it is the only source found that uses the name "merism", which no pre-1931 believing catalogue uses.
- Limit: it counts as one source.

## 6. Gaps

- **Merism** has no public-domain catalogue.
- **Character juxtaposition** has no catalogue at all. It must be built pair by pair from structures, Augustine and the commentators.
- **Chiasm and structure claims** often rest on Bullinger alone, which is "some interpreters" under the strength rule. The Layers build rule (layers.rs 409 to 411) would send such passages back.
recommendations: Use the FoS e-text (darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books @ 4017a67, the SQLite inside the zip) only to parse figure sections, bcv references and lettered structures. Check every word the app shows against the Princeton 1898 scan (figuresofspeechu00bull) and cite page numbers from it.

Write one mirror workflow modelled on .github/workflows/mirror-meaning-model.yml. It downloads the archive.org files (FoS Princeton and Cornell OCR and PDF, Companion Bible per-book OCR, Lowth 1829 and Isaiah 1834, Jebb 1820, Boys 1824 and 1825, Forbes 1854, Horne 1823 vol. 2), checks each against the sha1 that archive.org's metadata API lists (recorded in sources.md), and commits them to a branch such as mirror/literary-sources so sources.json can pin them.

Add Keach and De Laune's Tropologia (textcreationpartnership/A37483 @ e290ad3, CC0) to sources.json and to the layer-sources.json cite list as an interpreter. It is the only GitHub-native, cleanly licensed pre-1931 figure catalogue, and it covers anthropopatheia, prosopopoeia, synecdoche, hyperbole, metaphor and allegory.

Add Lowth, Jebb, Boys, Forbes and Horne to the cite list with not_on-style guards. For Lowth, cite his own words only, never the Michaelis or Stowe notes or the De Rossi chapter he translated. For Horne, only editions 1818 to 1846, never the 1856 Davidson volume.

Build Companion Bible structures by collating two OCRs (the Haywood CompanionBibleOT scan and the 1913 thecompanionbible_202504 per-book files). Check every member's verse range against the BSB and restore the matching (italic) members by letter. Do not show text from the UniqueBible notes module: it has OCR faults and the structures lost their letters.

Keep the strength rule as it is: count only writers who state the point themselves. Expect anthropopatheia, personification, antithetic parallelism and hyperbole notes to reach 3 or more writers among Calvin, Gill, Barnes, Clarke, JFB, Keil and Delitzsch, Pulpit, Benson, Wesley, Henry and Bullinger. Expect chiasm and inclusio notes to have 1 or 2 writers (Genesis 9:6 has none), so consider showing structures in their own extra rather than as Layers passages, which the layers.rs 'stronger than some interpreters' rule would send back.

For character juxtaposition, start from pairs that a believing source sets side by side in its own words. Examples: Companion Bible 1 Samuel 1:1 to 4:1 (Samuel against Eli's sons) and 1 Samuel 1:2 (Hannah and Peninnah, antimetabole); Augustine City of God XV.1 (Cain and Abel); Henry and Wesley on Genesis 4; JFB 'in contrast with Martha'. Never assert a foil from the story alone.

Add a build or review check that a Calvin citation from Bible Hub is not a Calvin Translation Society footnote. At Psalm 98:8 the 'most beautiful prosopopoeia' line is the translator's footnote [113], not Calvin.

Use Bullinger's own short definitions in Companion Bible Appendix 6 (181 figures, public domain) as the source for each device's one-line definition, rewritten in plain English with the source named. Note that Bullinger's 'Metaphor' is narrower than everyday usage (implied comparisons are 'Hypocatastasis') and his 'Merismos' is not the modern merism, so label devices by everyday names and give Bullinger's term at Deep.

Fix the link target while you are there: the 117 FoS cites point to the archive.org home page. Linking to the page (archive.org/details/figuresofspeechu00bull/page/N) would let readers see the figure Bullinger names.
founderQuestions: Bullinger would be the backbone of this feature (he is already cited 536 times). He held every word inspired, but also taught ultradispensationalism, soul sleep (close to a view Eusebius records an early synod correcting), the gap theory and the Gospel in the stars, and he chaired a flat-earth society meeting in 1905. Are you comfortable making him the main source for figures of speech and structures?

Is unfoldingWord's Translation Notes (modern, CC BY-SA 4.0, statement of faith says the Bible is 'the only inspired, inerrant, sufficient, authoritative Word of God', written by an unsigned team) acceptable as a source? It is the only one found that names merism and tags figures verse by verse.

Many chiasm and structure claims rest on one writer, often Bullinger alone, and Genesis 9:6, the best-known example, has no pre-1931 believing witness at all. Should single-writer structures be shown, labelled 'some interpreters', or held back?

May the build use the clean Figures of Speech and Companion Bible e-texts from GitHub repos that have no license and also contain copyrighted books? The texts themselves are public domain, and every displayed word would be checked against the 1898 scan. Or should we rely only on our own mirror of the archive.org scans?

Is Robert Lowth acceptable? He was a bishop who wrote that the sacred poems are 'justly attributed to the inspiration of the Holy Spirit', and he is the source of 'synonymous, antithetic, synthetic' parallelism. But his English editions carry notes by the German critic Michaelis, and his Isaiah includes his translation of a chapter by the Jewish scholar De Rossi.

Should devices be named in plain English at Simple (for example 'God described in human terms', 'a thing spoken of as a person', 'mirror order') with the classical names (Anthropopatheia, Prosopopoeia, Chiasmus) only at Study or Deep?

Where the sources split (Matthew 19:24 is 'hyperbole' to Ellicott but 'a proverb' to Barnes, Gill, Clarke and Bullinger), should the app show both labels with their writers, or pick the one most writers use?

## Codebase fit for literary devices (full write-up: C:\Users\shubh\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-shubh-Projects--claude\d3907c69-e0f0-457b-bec9-6a76569849b3\scratchpad\ba\literary\fit.md)

I read `origin/main` = `5296d48` after `git fetch`, using `git show` only. I made no edits, checkouts or commits in the clone. Another session fast-forwarded the local HEAD to `5296d48` while I worked; that was not me. The live site now serves build `7bd9f13db417`. None of the 44 remote branches has any code for this feature (I ran a git grep for chiasm, inclusio, anthropomorphism, parallelism, merism and `\q1`).

### Where it lives: three places, because the devices come in three shapes
1. **The BSB's own poetry lines go into the reader, as a core change, not an extra.** The build reads `\q1`, `\q2`, `\qr`, `\b` and `\d` from the already pinned `bsb-usfm` (usfm-bible/examples.bsb @ 48a9feb71f) and writes a book-level `poetry` field into `text/<Book>.json`. `Reader.tsx` (line 211, which draws `english` as one string) and `Pairs.tsx` `PairedEnglish` then draw each verse as its lines. This makes no claim and needs no writer. Extras can only add a line under a verse; they cannot change how a verse is drawn.
2. **Devices that sit in one verse become two new Layers kinds.** These are anthropomorphism and anthropopathism, personification, merism, hyperbole, metaphor and simile, and the parallelism inside one verse. The kinds are `figure` (field `figure` from a fixed list) and `parallelism` (field `form`: restated, opposite, building or climax, plus optional `lines`). `layers.rs` checks them like every other note. A new extra shows them as a line under the verse by reading `layers.json`, the same way `wordplay/model.ts` already does.
3. **Structures that span many verses get a new `structure` extra.** This covers chiasm, inclusio, alternation, refrains and foils. Files: `config/structures.json`, `crates/atlas-cli/src/extra_structure.rs`, `extras/structure.json` as the index and `extras/structure/<Book>.json` for detail. The panel shows a "ladder" of the members plus a small night-sky strip of nested arcs, built like `Roads.tsx` `NightStrip` with `gl/layout.ts` `arcPath`/`arcHeight`. Foils show in two columns through `parallels/Compare.tsx`. The map gets two new link kinds, `mirror` and `foil`, in `mapKinds.ts` and `colors.ts` `KIND`.

**Why structures cannot go into Layers as it stands:**
- All 1,264 live Layers passages are exactly one verse, and none overlap.
- `passageAt()` uses `Array.find`, and the card shows one passage. A chiasm passage such as Genesis 6:10 to 9:19 would hide, or be hidden by, the one-verse passages inside it.
- `layers.json` is fetched at boot (`App.tsx` line 121): 2,861,616 bytes raw, 626,287 gzipped, about 924 bytes raw (about 200 gzipped) per note.

### How the BSB USFM marks poetry (measured with tools/poetry.py)
- **Source checked:** the local copy of all 66 files matches the lock hashes. Psalms, Proverbs and Isaiah fetched again at the pinned commit are byte-identical.
- **Markers:** `\q2` 12,545; `\q1` 11,559; `\b` 3,953 stanza breaks; `\qr` 223 right-aligned refrains; `\d` 118 psalm titles; `\qa` 44 (the Psalm 119 letters).
  - There is no `\q3`, `\q4`, `\qc` or `\qm`, so the BSB uses two indent levels only.
  - The refrains are Selah 71, "declares the LORD." 62, "His loving devotion endures forever." 26 (every verse of Psalm 136), "And let all the people say, 'Amen!'" 12, and others.
- **Poetry verses:** 8,180 of the USFM's 31,084 (26.3%), in 55 books (OT 7,829, NT 351).
  - 8,150 (99.6%) split inside the verse, giving 24,823 lines.
  - Lines per verse: 1: 30, 2: 4,352, 3: 1,019, 4: 1,706, 5: 453, 6: 466, 7: 101, 8: 44, 9 or more: 9.
  - Only 8 verses begin mid-line: Judges 5:11, Psalms 55:3, 80:2, 96:13, Proverbs 26:24, Isaiah 28:12, Zechariah 12:1, Luke 1:74.
  - 442 verses start as prose and turn into poetry.
- **Coverage by book:** Psalms 2,459/2,461, Lamentations 153/154, Proverbs 895/915, Job 992/1,070, Hosea 181/197, Isaiah 1,121/1,292, Jeremiah 623/1,364, Ezekiel 197/1,273.
- **Placing the breaks on the English the app shows (BSB.json):**
  - 7,937 verses are identical.
  - 116 differ only because BSB.json joins the psalm title to verse 1 (Psalm 8:1 begins "For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. A Psalm of David.").
  - 127 differ in wording (the USFM is a fork as of 2024-08-26). Of these, 106 place cleanly with the word LCS already in `align.rs::pair` (line 111), accepting a break only on an exactly matched word. 21 cannot be placed.
  - 2 verses are broken in the USFM. Psalm 106:42 lost its `\v`, so its line is glued onto 106:41. Lamentations 2:1 is missing entirely.
  - Result: 8,159 of 8,182 poetry verses (99.7%) can be drawn as lines.
- **Hebrew and Greek in the same lines (tools/cola.py, 6,229 poetry verses in 11 books, using the live `row[2]` alignment):**
  - 86.0% split cleanly. By book: Proverbs 97.5%, Job 89.6%, Psalms 88.0%, Isaiah 76.5%.
  - Otherwise: word order crosses the lines (4.6%), one word's English is spread over two lines (4.3%), the alignment is partial (1.8%), or the English differs from the USFM (3.3%).
- **Antithetic lines are visible in the text:** in Proverbs 10 to 15, 147 of 183 two-line verses (80%) have a second line beginning with "but".
- **Cost of the line field:** 119,368 bytes raw, 31,408 gzipped across all books. Psalms adds 27,411 raw (+1.3% of its 2,162,131-byte shard) and 5,462 gzipped.

### What already exists that the feature can lean on
- **Bullinger:** *Figures of Speech* is on the cite list as an interpreter and already cited by 117 notes. The figure is named in the cite's `at`, for example "Anthropopatheia (Condescension)". Paronomasia 52, Ploce 23; Anthropopatheia, Hyperbole and Simile are rare.
- **Notes that frame a passage:** only one, the `pattern` note at 1 Samuel 2:10 (Hannah's and David's songs frame Samuel). No note mentions chiasm or inclusio.
- **Nave's (already pinned, parsed by `naves.rs::read`):**
  - ANTHROPOMORPHISMS defines the term and lists more than 60 passages under sub-headings: Walking (Genesis 3:8), Laughing (Psalm 2:4), Sleeping, Grieved (Genesis 6:6), Amazement.
  - It is hidden on the Themes tab by `naves-display.json` line 20.
  - It also has IRONY (19 references), POETRY and PERSONIFICATION.
- **Hard verse card:** `god-relents` (1 Samuel 15:29) is unreviewed; only its pointer shows, at Deep.
- **Founder's examples:** none of these verses has a Layers passage yet: Genesis 1:1, 4:4-5, 6:6, 25:27; 1 Samuel 1:2, 2:12, 2:26, 15:11; Luke 10:41, 18:11-14; Isaiah 53:1; Psalms 1:1, 8:1, 139:8. Genesis 4:2, 1 Samuel 15:29 and 16:7 do have passages, so a device note there must join the existing passage.
- **Bookends found by measurement:** 8 psalms have first and last verses sharing a run of 4 or more words: 8, 84, 103, 104, 118, 122, 136, 145.

### Checks the code already has, and how they would be reused
- **`layers.rs`:**

### What shows at each level
- **Simple:** verses in their BSB lines (titles on their own line, refrains set right, stanza gaps), plus one quiet line per device or structure.
- **Study:** Hebrew and Greek split into the same lines where the alignment allows; every note with its strength and word chips; the ladder with each member's text and its tying words underlined; foils in two columns; `mirror` and `foil` arcs on the map.
- **Deep:** the original words of each member with shared roots marked, the measured share per pair, evidence, sources with links, how each item was checked, and "Suggest a correction".

### Page weight
- Poetry lines: 31 KB gzipped in all, carried inside the text shards.
- Device notes in `layers.json`: about 200 B gzipped each, downloaded at boot.
- Structure index: about 15 to 20 KB raw for 300 structures (`parallels.json` holds 307 sets in 9,639 bytes).
- Structure detail: about 1 KB per structure, loaded when the panel opens.

### Risks
- The USFM differs from the text the app shows, so every line must be placed onto BSB.json and anything that does not fit dropped.
- Splitting the title off verse 1 is a visible change in 116 psalms.
- A chiasm is one writer's layout; writers often letter or centre the same passage differently.
- Structure sources from 1930 or earlier (Bullinger, Lowth, Jebb, Boys, Forbes) are not on GitHub in usable form. The only Bullinger-by-verse data found, github.com/kckern/IsaiahExplorer `public/com/bullinger.*.json`, covers Isaiah only and has no license file. Each source needs a mirror branch like `mirror-meaning-model.yml`.
- `shelf.rs` does not count citations from new config files, so new works would show no counts on the Sources shelf.
- There are no TypeScript tests beyond `tsc`, and the reader line drawing needs a check at phone width.

founderQuestions: Should verses show in the BSB's poetry lines at every level, including Simple (it is how the BSB itself prints them), or only from Study up?

BSB.json puts the psalm title at the start of verse 1 in 116 psalms (Psalm 8:1 begins 'For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. A Psalm of David.'). May the reader set the title on its own quiet line, as the printed BSB does?

A chiasm is usually one writer's layout, and writers letter or centre the same passage differently. Is it acceptable to show one layout 'as laid out by' its writer, with strength counting the writers who see a mirror with that same centre? Or should a structure appear only when 2 or more writers give the same members?

Away from the verses where a writer names the type of parallelism, should the app show only the lines with no label? In Proverbs 10 to 15, 80% of two-line verses have a second line beginning with 'but', but naming that 'opposites' would still need a writer under your rule.

May Nave's Topical Bible (Orville J. Nave, 1896, already used by the app) be added to the cite list as a reference for anthropomorphism? A note would still need an interpreter such as Bullinger, Gill or Keil and Delitzsch as well.

For structure, the public-domain Bible-believing writers are mainly Bullinger (1898, 1909-1922) and older Anglicans such as Lowth, Jebb, Boys and Forbes. May modern evangelical writers on structure also be cited and linked (never quoted at length), as Layers already cites Keener and Beale?
Should mirror and foil links on the map get new colors of their own, or reuse an existing one such as the lamp gold of theme threads?

For character juxtaposition, should a foil cover only pairs set side by side in one passage (Cain and Abel, Mary and Martha, the Pharisee and the tax collector)? Or also pairs that run across chapters, such as Saul and David across 1 Samuel 9 to 31?
